pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome  - Stormont House School - Achievement For All
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Stormont House School.
I hope our website gives you a sense of the vibrant, ambitious and caring community that makes our school such a special place to learn and belong.
At Stormont House, we work with young people aged 11-17 who have a range of special educational needs and disabilities. Every student who joins us brings their own strengths, interests, personality, and potential. By building positive relationships we are able to adapt our teaching and individualise our support. We recognise and nurture each student's talents, raise aspirations and help them achieve more than they may have thought possible.
Through high-quality teaching, personalised support and meaningful opportunities both inside and outside the classroom, we aim to equip our students with the knowledge, confidence and skills they need for positive relationships and fulfilling adult lives.
We have high expectations for all our students and are committed to ensuring they:
•Make exceptional progress in their learning, social development and emotional wellbeing.•Develop independence, resilience and the confidence to make informed choices about their future. [1]•Leave Stormont House ready for the next stage of education, employment or training, with qualifications, experiences and ambitions that reflect their individual goals and aspirations. [2]
Our students are at the heart of everything we do. We celebrate individuality and value the rich diversity of our school community. Our students bring unique perspectives, strengths and ways of understanding the world. We strive to create an environment where everyone feels safe, respected, included and empowered to be themselves.
The safety and wellbeing of our students will always be our highest priority. We are committed to safeguarding and to helping young people develop the skills, understanding and confidence they need to navigate the world successfully and safely.
I hope you enjoy finding out more about our school. Whether you are a prospective parent, carer, professional or visitor, I encourage you to explore our website and learn more about the opportunities we offer.
If you would like to know more, please visit our About Us and Curriculum pages, or get in touch with us directly. We would be delighted to hear from you.
Best wishes,Katie Foster
(She/Her) Headteacher Stormont House School
[1] Adapted from https://www.ndti.org.uk/resources/preparing-for-adulthood-all-tools-resources[2] Adapted from ‘Impact’ in the Education Inspection Framework

pageCache.text:
Our Vision, Values & Ethos
achievement for ALL IN A UNIQUE WORLD-CLASS SCHOOL
It means that our ultimate objectives for our students are for them to
Visitors notice and comment on the very strong and positive sense of community and belonging at our school. This relies on mutual respect, acceptance of difference, and valuing achievement in in all its forms. High levels of relational trust between students, between adults, and between students and adults are needed to enable individuals to flourish and surpass their previous personal best.
We celebrate the rich diversity of our students, many of whom are neurodiverse and approach interaction in unique way; every one of our students is normal, but not typical.
Every member of the school community has a right to be treated and valued equally regardless of their age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, or economic circumstances.
We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, including developing their own skills and awareness as they prepare for adulthood.
All of this sits well with the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs that we teach and promote in the curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers Partnerships - Stormont House School - Achievement For All
pageCache.text:
Careers Partnerships
SHS have been a Talentino School since 2019, Talentino are an early career development organisation created by senior people from business and education. They work across England in over 300 schools and projects with over 32,000 young people in scope so far.
They created a CEC SEND Strategy having identified the 9 key career challenges, they developed the SEND Gatsby Toolkit and have created several other SEND careers resources which are free to Schools. We as a school have benefited from being a part of a larger SEND Careers Network, having access to a Talentino LEAN Enterprise Co-ordinator, a wide variety of CPD training, access to SEND specific careers resources and invaluable support/challenge in developing a stable career programme & meeting the Gatsby Benchmarks.
We are a SEND Specialist member of the Hackney Careers Collaborative. The Careers Collaborative is an initiative that aims to ensure statutory duties around careers education information advice and guidance are met or exceeded. It is hosted and coordinated by Hackney Education but supports schools across London through online delivery. As a member of the Careers Collaborative the school have access to:
Events: Access to four collaborative events for students
Workshops and support: To improve student progression and provide CPD for staff supporting them
Careers Network Meetings: Six per annum
One to One Support Meetings: Members are offered three individual contact meetings, per annum. These can be used to discuss specific initiatives, address areas of concern or for sharing knowledge.
Resources: Bespoke resources include weekly careers and apprenticeship newsletters, monthly LMI, a calendar and bi-monthly bulletin to support CPD, careers education and careers guidance
Project Coordinator Support: Central coordination of collaborative activities and events, answers to enquiries and requests for bespoke support
The school's Careers Lead uses the information and CPD provided by the collaborative to enhance our schools’ careers offer and make sure we are meeting the 8 Gatsby Benchmarks.
The School Careers Lead is commissioned on behalf of the school to deliver a Vulnerable Groups Newsletter monthly for Collaborative members, which details current careers opportunities, information, and resources. The Careers Lead has in partnership with the Careers Collaborative delivered SEND focussed CPD for all Mainstream Hackney Schools and FE College members.
The Mayor of London wants every young person growing up in this city to have access to excellent careers education for a great start in life and a successful future. Building on the success of the London Enterprise Adviser Network (LEAN), Careers Hubs were launched in London in September 2021.
A Careers Hub is a group of secondary schools and colleges in a dedicated area that work together to deliver the Gatsby Benchmarks. Collaborating with business partners, the public, education, and voluntary sectors, they help deliver the Gatsby Benchmarks and improve careers outcomes for young people.
Stormont have been successful in becoming a part of the Central London Careers Hub, Led by Reed, in September 2021 as part of the first London Careers Hub cohort. This network has replaced LEAN for the school.
The Careers hub assigns each school an Enterprise Coordinator and Advisor. Our school's Enterprise Coordinator is Kirstie Hubbard and our Enterprise Advisor is Amy Packer who works for the construction company, Arc Group as a social value manager and has experience in delivering careers talks, employer and skills events and mock interviews to young people at schools, community groups and HE facilities. Amy set up the social value strategy for Arc Group along with a business plan and has a dedication to supporting young people. Amy is also a STEM Ambassador.
The Prince's Trust supports young people aged 11 to 30 who face disadvantage and adversity to move into work, education or training. Their programmes are designed to help young people raise their aspirations and move forwards with their lives, regardless of any challenges they may be facing.
At Stormont we are happy to count ourselves as one of the schools that The Prince's Trust deliver their programmes in. We currently access two programmes, Mosaic Mentoring and The Enterprise Challenge. Below is some information about those programmes:
Mosaic Mentoring
The Mosaic programme is one of The Prince’s Trust’s education programmes; Mosaic provides group mentoring and empowers 11 to 18 year olds to reach their full potential by connecting them with diverse and relatable role models from the world of work.
The key elements of the Mosaic Mentoring Programme are:
The Programme takes place primarily at school and is delivered by volunteer mentors recruited by The Prince’s Trust in accordance with all Disclosure and Barring Requirements.
a presentation by an external speaker
a visit to an external workplace
The Enterprise Challenge
The Enterprise Challenge programme is one of The Prince’s Trust’s education programmes; Enterprise Challenge is a school competition where young people are supported by trained volunteers to take on a range of challenges.
Pupils are in teams of 3 to 5 people throughout the Programme.
The key elements of the Programme are:
Prospects Services deliver impartial Careers Information Advice and Guidance that is independent of the School, thereby meeting the School’s Statutory obligations in accordance with the ‘Education Act 2011’ and ‘The Careers Guidance and access for education and training providers January 2023’. All students have access to a Level 6 SEND Careers Advisor from Prospects through 1-2-1 careers interviews, as well as the schools Prospects Advisor attending parents’ events and Annual Reviews when appropriate.
in-person mentoring by Prince’s Trust mentors
an online business simulation game

pageCache.text:
SEND Information Advice & Guidance
SENDIAGS stands for Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Information Advice and Guidance Service (they can also be known as SENDIASS). Most boroughs have at least one free, impartial, and confidential service offering information to young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) and to their parents and carers.
SENDIASS can support children, young people and their families on a range of issues including: school exclusions; EHC Needs Assessments; supporting conversations with a school or local authority; representation at SEND tribunals.
To find your local SENDIASS/SENDIAGS service visit here.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND Information Report - Stormont House School - Achievement For All
pageCache.text:
SEND Information Report
Our school is part of the Hackney Local Offer which is a good source of information about what is available locally and where.
Our school's SEND Information Report details the range of needs our school is designed to meet, our priorities, and how we are organised. Please find this report at the bottom of this page.
Stormont House is a secondary special school, so all our students have special educational needs and/or disabilities. They also arrive with untapped strengths and talents. It is our mission to address those needs but also to identify and nurture their interests and talents, challenging as well as supporting every student to prepare them for adulthood. We celebrate the rich diversity of our students, many of whom are neurodiverse and approach interaction in unique way; every one of our students is normal, but not typical.
Although students’ social communication, emotional and social development needs may impact on their behaviour at times, the school is not appropriate for social, emotional, and mental health difficulties or disorders that present an ongoing significant behavioural risk to self or others.
[1] Significant Speech, Language & Communication Needs (55-65%) or a diagnosis of Autism (40-45%)
[2] Adapted from https://www.ndti.org.uk/resources/preparing-for-adulthood-all-tools-resources
[3] Adapted from ‘Impact’ in the Education Inspection Framework

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnerships - Stormont House School - Achievement For All
pageCache.text:
Partnerships
We take great pride in our extensive network of partners, covering all key areas; business, education, community and culture on a local, national and international level. Each of our partnerships contribute to and enrich our curriculum offer for students and form an integral part of our unique and inspiring learning environment.
In our mission to raise aspirations and support young people to be prepared for adulthood, we utilise our partnerships and networks to further enhance the curriculum and give students an insight into the working world. Aside from providing exciting opportunities, our partnerships allow for personal development, encourage reflective practice and most importantly inspire students.
These strong collaborative partnerships enrich our curriculum offer and provide students with opportunities which support and enhance their learning including trips, speakers, visits and mentoring. Above all, the partnership activities broaden our students’ horizons, taking their learning beyond the classroom and providing a unique insight.
Our partnerships enable us to use our expertise to give back and collaborate with our partners by sharing good practice, delivering training, supporting by giving advice and guidance.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chefs in Schools & Hackney School of Food - Stormont House School - Achievement For All
pageCache.text:
Chefs in Schools & Hackney School of Food
Chefs in schools are an amazing organisation who aim to transform school food and food education. They work with chefs from the commercial sector to develop fresh and flavourful food options on a tight school budget. Some of this involves staff training, sharing expertise and also sourcing high-quality produce at a manageable cost. Charles Gabriel, our Chef Educator, is an Urban Food Awards prize-winner in his own right having been trained by Chefs in Schools after joining us from the commercial sector. He and his team adapted the Chefs in Schools' menus and also contributed to them. To reduce our carbon footprint and support a more sustainable food chain, we have two meat-free days per week in school. This also allows us to buy meat and fish of very high quality for the other 3 days of the week. To find out more about Chefs in Schools, please see their website here.

East London Teaching School Hub
The East London Teaching School Hub is one of 87 Teaching School Hubs designated by the Department for Education.
As the Hub for Hackney and Tower Hamlets, East London Teaching School Hub (ELTSH) is responsible for ensuring teachers from all state-funded schools in our region have access to the best quality evidence-informed teacher development programmes at every stage of their career.
Collaboration is a key part of the East London Teaching School Hub’s approach so we work with a range of school leaders and key strategic partners, who bring with them a wealth of expertise and experience, to ensure the programmes we collectively offer meet our local context.
An ethos of collegiality, inclusion and transparency guide our partnership work. Together, we change lives by providing the highest quality teacher development opportunities.

HTSA
The Hackney Teaching & Schools' Alliance (HTSA) is a supportive partnership of primary, secondary, special and alternative provision schools, each with a proven track record of successful improvement. The alliance work together to improve the quality of teaching and leadership through effective collaboration and personalised support.
HTSA member schools and their staff have preferential access to high-quality professional development programmes.The HTSA is steered by an Executive Board chaired by the Headteacher of Stormont House School, working closely with Clapton Girls' Academy, Millfields Community School and The LEAP Federation of Kingsmead, Mandeville and Gayhurst Schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers & Employment - Stormont House School - Achievement For All
pageCache.text:
Careers & Employment
At Stormont House School and Sixth Form we aim to raise the aspirations of all our students while equipping them with the knowledge, confidence, skills, and attributes to achieve their full potential. It is important that students are enabled to make informed decisions about post 16 routes and the relevant pathways to support their longer-term future career plans. To enable our students to achieve we deliver an embedded programme of careers education and guidance in Key Stage 3, 4 and 5 which has been developed to deliver the SEND Gatsby Benchmarks, meet the Careers Statutory Guidance 2023 and is informed by the National Careers Strategy 2017.
We are committed to providing a well-structured Careers Education, Information Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) for all students in Year 7 to 12. We strive to ensure students experience a full, varied and interesting careers journey, having the opportunity to explore their own interests, skills, and passions; understanding the wealth of jobs and education available to them once they leave school. It is integrated into our students’ experience across the whole curriculum and is based on a partnership with, students and their parents or carers. We have a rich partnership with local businesses, colleges and providers along with a strong alumni and wider school community to support our Careers Education.
We work in partnership with Prospects Careers Service, Talentino, Hackney Careers Collaborative, the Central London Careers Hub and many other organisations that support us as a school to grow our careers programme so that it is progressive and creates opportunities for our students in the ever changing job market.
For further information, or if you are a business or organisation that would like to engage with us in delivering our Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG), please contact:
Ms Claire Napier (Sixth Form and Careers Lead)
